name: plan-phases-project-scoping
body:
`apg_plan_phases` (the suite tool `opencode-suite/tools/apg_plan_phases.ts`) reports exactly the requirements the CURRENT project / branch is responsible for, rather than every requirement in the layers store. The tool loads all `Requirement` nodes (line 41: `MATCH (r:Requirement) RETURN r.fqn`) and flags any lacking a `Satisfies` edge as unsatisfied (line 82). A project's plan is transient and dies with its branch, so requirements delivered by earlier projects keep zero surviving `Satisfies` edge and read unsatisfied forever (observed in apg-cleanup: 24-25 earlier-delivered requirements). The tool scopes the requirement set to the project.

IN SCOPE (decided): a requirement is in scope for the current project/branch when it is BRANCH-ADDED or is SATISFIED by one of this project's phases — in-scope = branch-added requirements ∪ requirements this project's phases Satisfy. Branch-added mirrors the binary's `solution_nodes_added_on_branch` (`rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.solution_nodes_added_on_branch`, `src/plan_cmd/verify.rs` lines 240-287): a `apg/layers/requirements/requirement/<name>.json` node file present on this branch but absent from the repo's default branch. The suite tool may shell out to git to compute this (the shared lib already runs subprocesses via `Bun.$` for `apg query`). The design splits cleanly across the test tiers: the scoping DECISION is a PURE function in the shared `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` — given the full requirement FQN set, the branch-added set, and this project's `Satisfies` phase FQNs, it returns the in-scope set and the findings — and is covered by the bun unit tier in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts`; the git branch-delta shell-out is a thin subprocess WRAPPER around that pure core (a subprocess is real I/O, hence e2e, rather than unit) and is covered by the opt-in suite e2e. The tool's top-level logic is a default-exported `tool({...})` and works outside direct unit-test; the pure core lives in the shared lib.

FINDINGS after the change:
- Preserved: the empty-tasks finding; the done-but-under-review finding; the Gates-cycle finding.
- `!! unsatisfied requirements` = in-scope requirements lacking a `Satisfies` edge from a phase of THIS project (equivalently, branch-added requirements the project's plan leaves unsatisfied).
- `!! <req> Satisfied by more than one phase` = requirements Satisfied by more than one phase OF THIS PROJECT (the `Satisfies` lookup filtered to this project's phases).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Running `apg_plan_phases` in a project whose branch adds zero requirement and whose plan satisfies its own requirements reports zero unsatisfied finding for requirements delivered by other projects; the in-scope set is exactly {requirements added on this branch} ∪ {requirements this project's phases Satisfy}.
- A branch-added requirement lacking a satisfying phase is still reported unsatisfied; a requirement satisfied by two phases of the project is still reported over-satisfied.
- The empty-tasks, done-but-under-review and Gates-cycle findings are unchanged.
- Test tiers, split exactly: the PURE scoping core in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` (requirement FQNs + branch-added set + this project's `Satisfies` phase FQNs -> in-scope set and findings) is covered by the side-effect-free bun unit tier in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts`; the git branch-delta shell-out wrapper is covered by the opt-in suite e2e (`opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`) against a scratch `/tmp` repo per the self-contained-tests law.
- The two Rust e2e regressions stay green: `full_dogfood_round_trip_suite_tool_ops_inside_the_worktree` (`tests/project_cmd_e2e.rs`) and `suite_tools_query_error_guard_is_structural` (`tests/main_e2e.rs`, which structurally pins `apg_plan_phases.ts`'s try/catch/`csvToRows`/return shape); the scoping change leaves both green.
- Non-goal: zero change to the `apg` binary and zero change to suite tools other than `apg_plan_phases` and the shared-lib helper it uses (see `requirements.constraint.plan-tooling-change-boundary`).

KNOWN CONSEQUENCE: `opencode-suite/agents/plan-writer.md` (line 213) relies on `apg_plan_phases` reporting unsatisfied requirements for its self-review; with this scoping that check becomes project-local.
